claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic mixture of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti elemental powders.
Six hours of high-energy ball milling produces severe lattice strain and nanoscale grain refinement.
Milling-induced lattice strain and grain refinement lower the activation-energy barrier for an FCC-to-BCC solid-solution transition.
SPS at 1000°C facilitates densification of the milled CoCrFeNiTi powder.
SPS at 1000°C stabilizes the refined BCC structure.
SPS at 1000°C avoids excessive Ti-driven HCP precipitation.
A VEC above a critical threshold favors BCC stability in equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti tends to segregate and form HCP phases during thermal processing of CoCrFeNiTi.
An inert argon milling atmosphere prevents oxidation.
VEC and atomic-radius mismatch govern final FCC/BCC phase selection in CoCrFeNiTi.
Six hours of milling introduces a high dislocation density.
Milling increases the configurational-entropy contribution relative to the enthalpy of mixing.
The BCC phase is entropically stabilized around 1000°C for the VEC of CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed process yields less than 2% porosity.
The proposed process yields a single-phase or dominant BCC solid solution with negligible HCP phase.
Milling-induced grain refinement increases Vickers hardness through Hall–Petch strengthening.
Atomic-size mismatch produces solid-solution strengthening and contributes to higher hardness in a BCC matrix.
As-cast CoCrFeNiTi has coarse dendritic microstructures and segregation.
Sintering above approximately 1100°C causes rapid grain growth or phase decomposition that negates Hall–Petch strengthening.
Vickers hardness testing at 0.1 kgf isolates grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as an elemental powder mixture but is simultaneously assigned porosity and coarse-grain characteristics typical of an as-cast or arc-melted bulk precursor; these are distinct starting states.

The mediator frames milling as lowering a kinetic activation barrier through strain and refinement, whereas the mechanism attributes the transition to milling increasing configurational entropy relative to mixing enthalpy. The latter is a thermodynamic claim and is not clearly reconciled with the kinetic-barrier account.
